title: Insurance Claims and Service Advisor
description:
Claims & Service Adviser
Shoeburyness, Essex £26,000-£28,000, with flexibility for the right experience Full-time, office-based

Do you have insurance claims or customer service experience and enjoy helping customers, solving problems and seeing cases through to resolution?

CKB Recruitment is working with an established insurance business to recruit a Claims & Service Adviser for its team in Shoeburyness.

Covering gadget insurance, travel insurance and ticket protection, this varied role will give you the opportunity to broaden your knowledge across several products. You'll handle claims, sales enquiries, policy servicing and first-line complaints, taking ownership and working closely with colleagues to deliver a positive customer experience.

You'll join an open, collaborative business where people are encouraged to share ideas, ask questions and help improve how things are done.

The salary, benefits and working environment
- £26,000-£28,000 basic salary, depending on experience, with a higher salary potentially available for the right candidate, particularly someone with closely relevant insurance experience.
- 22 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- The opportunity to earn up to three additional days' holiday through the company's non-sickness policy.
- The opportunity to earn up to three further days' holiday through length of service.
- A welcoming, open-plan office with fresh fruit, biscuits and snacks provided weekly, plus a new coffee machine.
- Opportunities to develop your knowledge across multiple insurance products, with cross-training in ticket protection.
- A collaborative culture that welcomes initiative and suggestions.

What you'll be doing

You'll work across claims and customer service, helping customers understand their options and keeping cases moving towards resolution.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Handling mobile phone and gadget claims involving loss, theft and accidental damage, including cover provided alongside travel insurance.
- Managing ticket protection claims and refund requests once cross-trained.
- Responding to travel, mobile phone and gadget insurance sales and service enquiries.
- Liaising with underwriters on travel-related product queries.
- Working with repair and fulfilment colleagues to progress and conclude claims.
- Processing premium and excess payments.
- Managing policy cancellations and retention conversations.
- Recording and handling first-line complaints in line with company procedures.
- Working with finance colleagues on payment and reconciliation queries.
- Supporting colleagues across the business and suggesting improvements to processes and customer service.

What we're looking for

Previous claims or customer service experience within a regulated insurance business is essential.

You'll be customer-focused, enthusiastic and keen to develop your insurance knowledge, with the confidence to take responsibility for a varied workload.

You'll also need:
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with confidence on the telephone and by email.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- A positive, hardworking and self-motivated approach.
- The ability to manage multiple products, tasks and priorities in a busy, evolving environment.
- A proactive mindset and willingness to ask questions and contribute ideas.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel.

Experience handling complaints, investigating potential fraud or working in additional languages would be beneficial, although these are not essential.

Location and working hours

This role is fully office-based in Shoeburyness, with close day-to-day collaboration between the manager and team. Hybrid working is not available.

Working hours are:
- Monday-Wednesday: 9:00am-5:30pm.
- Thursday-Friday: 9:00am-5:00pm.

An immediate start is available.

If you're looking for a varied insurance role where you can develop your knowledge and take ownership of the customer experience, apply with your CV or contact CKB Recruitment for a confidential conversation.

title: Procurement Administrator
description:
Job Title: Procurement Administrator

Location: Waltham Abbey, Essex

Working Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am - 5:30pm

Working Arrangement: 100% Office Based

Role Purpose

The Procurement Administrator will provide day-to-day support to the Procurement Manager and wider business, assisting with purchasing activities and ensuring orders are processed accurately, efficiently, and in line with company procedures.

The role will involve managing purchase orders, liaising with suppliers, maintaining accurate procurement records, and supporting the purchase of mobile phones, devices, accessories, and other business requirements.

Working closely with internal teams, Finance, and external suppliers, the Procurement Administrator will help ensure purchasing requirements are fulfilled on time, within budget, and in accordance with company policies, approval processes, and procurement standards.

This is a fully office-based role in Waltham Abbey and requires an individual with previous purchasing, buying, procurement, or supply chain experience.

Key Responsibilities
- Raise, process, and manage purchase orders in line with company procurement procedures and approval processes.
- Assist with the procurement of mobile phones, devices, accessories, and other business requirements.
- Obtain supplier quotations and compare pricing, availability, and delivery times to support cost-effective purchasing decisions.
- Liaise with suppliers to confirm pricing, place orders, and monitor delivery timescales.
- Track outstanding orders and proactively follow up with suppliers regarding delays, shortages, discrepancies, or damaged goods.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date procurement records, including purchase orders, supplier details, quotations, and pricing.
- Update and maintain procurement systems, databases, and spreadsheets, ensuring information is accurate and current.
- Work closely with the Finance team to resolve invoice queries, pricing discrepancies, and payment-related issues.
- Ensure all purchasing activity is carried out in line with company policies, agreed budgets, and relevant approval processes.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Identify and escalate purchasing issues, risks, or discrepancies to the Procurement Manager in a timely manner.
- Provide general administrative and day-to-day support to the Procurement Manager and wider team as required.
- Assist with maintaining accurate supplier and product information to support efficient purchasing activity.
- Support the wider Procurement function with administrative and operational tasks as required.

Essential Experience and Skills
- Previous experience in purchasing, buying, procurement, supply chain, or a similar commercial environment is essential.
- Experience of raising and managing purchase orders.
- Experience liaising with suppliers and obtaining quotations.
- Good understanding of purchasing and order management processes.
- Strong administrative and organisational skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Ability to manage multiple orders and priorities effectively.
- Confident communicating with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Good numerical and commercial awareness, with the ability to compare pricing and identify discrepancies.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook.
- Ability to maintain accurate records and work within established procedures and approval processes.
- Proactive approach to following up outstanding orders and resolving purchasing issues.
- Ability to work effectively as part of a team while also managing individual responsibilities.

Please be aware this advert will remain open until the vacancy has been filled. Interviews will take place throughout this period, therefore we encourage you to apply early to avoid disappointment.

Tate is acting as an Employment Business in relation to this vacancy.

Tate is committed to promoting equal opportunities. To ensure that every candidate has the best experience with us, we encourage you to let us know if there are any adjustments we can make during the application or interview process. Your comfort and accessibility are our priority, and we are here to support you every step of the way. Additionally, we value and respect your individuality, and we invite you to share your preferred pronouns in your application.

title: Commercial Claims Handler
description:
Our Client, an Insurance Broker, is looking to recruit another Commercial Claims Handler to join their friendly and growing team.

This is a great opportunity to develop your Claims Handling knowledge and skills into handling a wide variety of Commercial Claims.

It's your ability to deal with claimants and handle all aspects of Claims activities that is most important - specific technical class knowledge can be learnt.

- Ensuring claims are processed within agreed standard practices and procedures
- Creating and maintaining Claims files electronically
- Advising, updating and where necessary negotiating open market Claims
- Communicating with carriers, third parties and service providers
- Ensuring that all financial aspects are handled in a timely manner

To be successful as a Commercial Claims Handler in this role you will have:
- Claims Handling experience
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills
- Strong work ethic and customer focus with a drive to achieve best possible settlements
- Ability to convey a professional and confident image

title: Claims Handler
description:
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Claims professional to join our Client's growing team. They are market leaders and growing their business strongly and keen to continue to add more talented people into their friendly team.

The role involves handling a very wide variety of Liability claims (including Professional Indemnity, Employment Liability, Public Liability) for a wide variety of clients, who they have a close and long standing relationships with.

You'll be an experienced Claims Handler and a strong negotiator who is comfortable working closely with Solicitors and discussing settlements. Also in a hands-on Technical role involving policy interpretation, liability assessment, and negotiation.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone looking to step into a role where you'd be challenged with a range of complex Claims issues and with strong technical and client service exposure.

Our Client is very focused on professional training and career development; they support your professional qualifications and provide progression opportunities.

The responsibilities of the Claims Handler role will include:
- Managing a caseload of claims, investigating the details of each claim, assessing the claims against the policy terms and conditions.
- Conducting thorough investigations by contacting relevant parties and reviewing documentation.
- Identifying potential fraud or suspicious claims and report
- Negotiating and managing fee agreements with Claimants' representatives.
- Communicating claim status updates to policyholders/partners regularly, ensuring transparency throughout the process.

To be a successful Claims Handler you will demonstrate:
- Experience handling Liability claims.
- Strong negotiation, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities to assess claim details and make informed decisions.
- Detail-oriented with the ability to manage a high volume of claims accurately and efficiently.

Initially to facilitate your training and to enable you to build your internal network, you will be full-time office-based, after which you can work on a hybrid basis.

title: Property Inspections Team Coordinator
description:
Property Inspections Team Coordinator

Location: Chelmsford / Hybrid
Salary: £25,000 - £28,000 + bonuses
Full-time Permanent No weekends

We are currently recruiting for a Property Inspections Team Coordinator to join the busy property management and inspections team of a highly successful and established independent estate agency.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced residential lettings professional looking to develop their career within property administration, inspections and tenancy management.

Following successful completion of the initial probationary period, the role will become hybrid, offering a combination of home and office-based working.

The Role

As Property Inspections Team Coordinator, you will provide essential administrative and coordination support to the property inspections team, helping to ensure appointments, inventories, compliance requirements and tenancy deposits are managed efficiently.

You will work closely with Property Inspection Consultants, inventory clerks, branches, landlords, tenants and internal teams, playing a key role in keeping the department organised and ensuring appointments and processes run smoothly.

Key Responsibilities

Coordinate and book property inspection visits and check-out appointments.
Send reminder communications to tenants moving out.
Update property management systems with meter readings, appliances and smoke/CO alarm information from inventories.
Rearrange property visits and manage changes to appointments.
Monitor group emails and handle calls when Property Inspection Consultants are unavailable.
Manage Property Inspection Consultants' diaries and agency bookings.
Arrange deposit releases and submit relevant documentation to accounts.
Assist with deposit negotiations between landlords and tenants.
Process relevant paperwork for independent deposit adjudication where required.
Manage information across third-party CRM systems relating to inventories and condition reports.
Monitor incoming inventories and ensure compliance requirements are met.
Liaise with progressors and branches where there are issues affecting compliance or property readiness.
Coordinate last-minute inventory appointments between inventory clerks and branches.
Download and distribute completed inventories to landlords.
Support the Team Leader with day-to-day departmental tasks.
Maintain accurate records and ensure all processes are completed efficiently and within required timescales.

About You

We are looking for an organised and proactive property professional with previous experience within residential lettings.

You should have:

Current or previous experience within residential lettings - essential.
Excellent organisational and prioritisation skills.
A proactive "can-do" attitude.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
A personable, outgoing and enthusiastic approach.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
The ability to work independently while also contributing effectively as part of a team.
Good IT skills and confidence using Microsoft Office.
The ability to learn and adapt quickly to new technology and property management systems.
A professional and customer-focused approach.

Salary & Benefits

£25,000 - £28,000 basic salary, depending on skills and industry experience, plus bonuses.

The role also offers:

Hybrid working following probation.
Birthday day off.
Company pension.
Training and development opportunities.
Regular company events.
Financial referral programme.
Performance-related bonuses.
Retail vouchers and rewards for outstanding performers.
Additional benefits linked to length of service.
Excellent opportunities for career progression.

Working Hours

Monday - Friday: 8:30am - 5:30pm

No weekend working.

Following successful completion of the probationary period, the role will operate on a hybrid basis:

3 days at Head Office in Chelmsford + 2 days working from home.

Apply Now

If you have experience within residential lettings, property management, tenancy administration or estate agency and are looking for a varied coordination role with an established and supportive property business, we would love to hear from you.

Apply today for a confidential conversation about this opportunity.

title: Commercial Claims Handler
description:
Our Client, an Insurance Broker, is looking to recruit another Commercial Claims Handler to join their friendly and growing team.

This is a great opportunity to develop your Claims Handling knowledge and skills into handling a wide variety of Commercial Claims.

It's your ability to deal with claimants and handle all aspects of Claims activities that is most important - specific technical class knowledge can be learnt.

You'll be at the heart of the Broker's Claims service, delivering confident, proactive support to Commercial clients and their claims. They handle all types of Commercial Insurance, and their client base spans Property, EL, PL, PI, Cyber, D&O.

You will also be able to attend renewal meetings with your Account Executives, and the occasional quarterly Claims meetings.

You'll work closely with the rest of the Commercial team including Handlers and Execs, who will value your help and support - as will your clients.

Your main responsibilities as a Commercial Claims Handler will include:
- Receiving and actioning Claims instructions in a timely manner
- Negotiating to reach the best settlement possible for our clients whilst maintaining a good relationship with Insurers
- Liaise and advise clients, colleagues and insurers on claims procedures, queries and technical liability queries
- Ensuring claims are processed within agreed standard practices and procedures
- Creating and maintaining Claims files electronically
- Obtaining Claims agreement as per contract conditions or within appropriate timescales to ensure secure, efficient, and auditable handling of client monies
- Communicating with carriers, third parties and service providers

To be successful as a Commercial Claims Handler in this role you will have:
- Claims Handling experience
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills
- Strong work ethic and customer focus with a drive to achieve best possible settlements
- Ability to convey a professional and confident image

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Finance Assistant / Colchester / Salary £25,000-£30,000 (DOE) & Benefits

A growing, successful and well-established family-owned educational supplies business is looking to hire a Finance Assistant at their Colchester Head Office.

The role would be ideal for someone who is the early stages of their financial career or a recent graduate and is looking to gain experience in a hands-on role. This is an exciting opportunity to join a key company in the educational supplies sector that has a been at the forefront of the industry for over 50 years.

With a client base that exceeds 3,000 schools across the South East, HBS Group is focussed on continuing to strengthen their product offering which already spans over 15,000 products as well as optimising procurement operations and fostering innovation in product development.

Key Responsibilities of the Finance Assistant:
- Support the day-to-day finance function and ensure accurate and timely financial administration.
- Process purchase and sales invoices, expenses and payment requests.
- Maintain accurate financial records and assist with account reconciliations.
- Assist with accounts payable and accounts receivable activities.
- Prepare and process supplier payments and resolve invoice queries.
- Monitor outstanding customer and supplier balances.
- Assist with monthly management accounts and financial reporting.
- Support month-end and year-end accounting processes.
- Reconcile bank, credit card and other balance sheet accounts.
- Assist with maintaining the finance system and ensuring data accuracy.
- Provide financial information and reports to management when required.
- Liaise with suppliers, customers and internal departments regarding financial queries.
- Ensure finance processes comply with company policies and relevant regulations.
- Support the Finance Manager with ad-hoc analysis and administrative tasks.

Skills and Experience Required:
- Good understanding of basic accounting principles.
- Strong attention to detail and numerical accuracy.
- Good organisational and time-management skills.
- Confident using Excel and financial/accounting systems.
- Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- Good communication and interpersonal skills.
- A proactive, reliable and collaborative approach.
- Ability to handle confidential financial information appropriately.

What's in it for you:
- Permanent full-time position
- Salary £25,000-£30,000 per annum (DOE) Plus Company Bonus Plan
- Statutory pension and 25 days holiday + bank holidays
- Free Parking and staff BBQ's
- A friendly and positive team working environment and culture

description: Medical Secretary Administrator Are you looking for a rewarding administrative role within the NHS, where your work makes a real difference to patient care?
